newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES EASE, LITHUANIAN GAS PLUMMETS.
newsitem.headline: SHARES EASE, LITHUANIAN GAS PLUMMETS.

text.p: * Lithuanian shares continued to ease on Wednesday.
* Lithuanian Gas fell sharply for the second straight session, dropping to 1.79 litas from 1.98 litas.
* The Baltic Shipyard eased to 7.55 litas from 8.55 litas.
Lithuanian Gas fell sharply for the second straight session as most blue chips eased on Lithuania's bearish bourse, dealers said.
Dealers said that investors were still waiting for first quarter results and that depressed prices elsewhere in Eastern Europe were dragging Lithuanian shares down.
Lithuanian Gas dropped 9.60 percent to 1.79 litas and dealers were not bullish about the state-run gas giant's immediate prospects.
"Judging from the order's list, Lithuanian Gas should fall some more," said Tomas Andrejauskas of brokerage house Suprema.
The company recently reported that its 1996 losses were at least 78 million litas.
The Baltic Shipyard also eased, sinking to 7.55 litas from 8.55 litas.
Its price rose rapidly last week after Denmark's Odense Shipyard bought 43 percent of its shares in a block deal on the Vilnius bourse.
"It's a normal after such a big increase for the price of a company to start falling again," said Andrejauskas.
Final resluts from Wednesday's session, including indexes and trade volumes, will be available later in the day.
